subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real function log(x² − 4x + 3).

mark_split.label: Condition for the function to be defined

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.81 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 96.1, on ★★★ SSP 81 (the book calls it 'the most dominating domain page'). Appearance years are printed board-split. UNLIKE the LAQ and SAQ pages, the book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages: the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the condition the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the condition
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the condition alone. Write it before any factorising.

recall.must_convey: That a logarithm needs its input STRICTLY greater than zero — not greater than or equal — so x² − 4x + 3 > 0.
accept: log needs the inside strictly positive so x squared minus four x plus three greater than zero
the argument of the logarithm must be positive not zero
for log the inside has to be strictly greater than zero
log ki inside strictly positive undali zero kaadu
set the quadratic strictly greater than zero because it is a log

steps.why: log 0 is undefined and log of a negative number is not real, so the input must be strictly positive — this is the one place the bracket type changes.
common_mistakes: Using ≥ 0, the square-root condition, which wrongly lets in the points where the input is zero.
Factorising to (x − 1)(x − 4) and moving the second root.

steps.label: Write the domain
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the interval itself. Write it in interval form, and check every bracket.

recall.must_convey: That the answer uses OPEN brackets: minus infinity to 1, union 3 to infinity, endpoints excluded.
accept: minus infinity to one union three to infinity with open brackets
x less than one or greater than three strictly
open intervals because log of zero is undefined
one kanna takkuva or three kanna ekkuva strictly
the two open intervals outside one and three

steps.why: Because the inequality is strict, 1 and 3 are excluded, so every bracket here is round.
common_mistakes: Writing square brackets at 1 and 3, where log is undefined.
Giving the middle interval (1, 3), where the input is negative.
